nodes.claim: The perfect genetic axiom imports genomes people already have; it never assays.
nodes.detail: An assay pipeline (samples, labs, clinical accreditation) is a different institution, not a harder feature. Consumer raw files (23andMe/AncestryDNA class, hundreds of thousands of genotyped positions) already exist in the hands of exactly the people most likely to bring them, and importing keeps the perfect system on the analysis side, where its comparative advantage (the phenotype battery, gen-3) actually is. Even in the no-practical-limits frame, assaying adds custody and liability without adding analytical power the imported file lacks for trait work.

nodes.claim: In the perfect system the genome stays where the person is; only derived, banded quantities travel.
nodes.detail: Device-side scoring against published weight sets gives the crowd half everything it needs (score bands) while the raw sequence never enters anyone's custody. This is not a privacy compromise on the perfect design — it IS the perfect design, because a genome is unrevokable and familial (gen-6): minimizing custody is minimizing irreversible failure modes, and a system with fewer irreversible failure modes is better on pure design grounds. Open question for a future run: what the ceiling of device-side analysis is (imputation quality without a server, structural variants, polygenic interaction terms).

nodes.claim: The scarce asset is the phenotype battery, not the genotypes; the perfect axiom is designed around that asymmetry.
nodes.detail: Genotypes are commodity files; deep, longitudinal, freely-given phenotypes are what biobanks cannot buy cheaply. InSight's answer corpus is an unusually rich behavioral phenotyping instrument. The perfect genetic axiom therefore optimizes for pairing quality (how many people have BOTH a scored genome and a deep phenotype record) over genotype count, and treats every phenotype-side improvement (questions axiom) as a genetic-axiom improvement. Ranking claim for central: this asymmetry is the genetic axiom's main contribution to the combination. External support arrived with gen-4's scout (2026-08-25): the education–pace-of-aging association in Framingham (DunedinPACE analysis n=3,101, drawn from a three-generation mobility database of n=14,106) holds under within-family sibling fixed effects and across four alternative clocks (Graf 2024, cited at gen-4) — behavioral phenotype carries aging signal that shared family background alone does not explain, which is this asymmetry stated by someone else's data. A future run may raise this node on that basis after full-text verification; note the stronger 'survives polygenic-index adjustment' reading of Graf did NOT survive this run's adversarial check (unconfirmable from the abstract) — the sibling-fixed-effects reading did, and it is the one recorded here. Raised argued→cited 2026-08-27: the instrument premise — that a bank of self-report items is a genetic-grade phenotyping instrument — now has direct external demonstrations. A single well-chosen self-report item carries a genetically valid phenotype at scale: musical beat synchronization, one self-report item in n=606,825, yielded 69 genome-wide-significant loci with SNP-h2 13–16%, and the item was validated against separate experimental rhythm-perception and beat-synchronization measures in independent participants (Niarchou 2022). Web-based participant-driven self-report phenotyping is the founding method of consumer-cohort genetics (Eriksson 2010: 22 self-report traits, ~10,000 participants, novel replicated associations including photic sneeze and asparagus anosmia). Aggregation raises the genetic signal: interest heritability ~32% at item level rises to ~48% at factor and ~53% at superfactor level (Lykken 1993, twin-based) — so the perfect battery scores constructs over many items, which is what a deep answer corpus does by design. And the interests half of the battery is a genuine open frontier, stated precisely after the adversarial pass (which refuted this sentence's first draft): vocational interests are heritable at twin grade (~36% genetic in the combined twin/adoption design of Betsworth 1994; ~36–50% across twin studies), and while NO GWAS of an administered interest INVENTORY (Strong/RIASEC-class) was found, behavioral and educational proxies for interests HAVE been GWASed and show the signal is there — educational-field choice across 463,134 individuals yields 17 genome-wide-significant variants across 7 of 10 fields at mean SNP-h2 ~7%, with signal specific to field choice rather than educational level, and its two recovered latent dimensions (technical-vs-social, practical-vs-abstract) are the axes underlying Holland's RIASEC interest hexagon (Cheesman 2025); STEM occupational choice gives 2 loci at SNP-h2 4.2% (Human Genomics 2023). A deep, inventory-grade interests phenotype paired with imported genotypes would still be first of its kind — and the proxies say it would find something. Provenance note for this rise: the run's environment blocked publisher pages, so sources were verified as real at record grade (consistent title/venue/identifier across independent index records) and figures are snippet-grade unless stated. RE-WARRANTED 2026-09-03 (SCHEMA's go-12 rule; flagged by the review lane's Connected finding and by the health instrument): cen-1 changed on 2026-08-28 from one shared latent space into two linked geometries — a between-person geometry every axiom measures into, plus within-person state geometries with their own loadings, published as aggregate sufficient statistics. This edge survives, narrowed to the between-person layer: the battery is the scarce asset for pairing coverage there, while the within-person geometry is funded by occasions (pat-8) and takes no genotype limb at all (gen-18). Read as a claim about the joint model entire, this node would overstate itself.

nodes.claim: The aging ambition runs through behavior-by-aging-measure crosses over the phenotype battery — the genotype contributes a weak prior, and discovery genetics stays out of scope.
nodes.detail: Scouted and adversarially checked 2026-08-25 (14 refutation searches; fixes applied before landing — see LOG). Provenance, per figure: sources were verified to exist via multiple independent indexes; the skeptic pass then confirmed against source-side text the 0.47% GrimAge instrument strength (4 SNPs), MIMOSA's 0.20 average imputation correlation, Timmers' ~5-year decile gap, Graf's n=3,101 analysis / n=14,106 database, and TruDiagnostic's n=14,213; the 4.41% upper instrument figure remains abstract-grade pending full text. Three findings ground the restated claim. (1) The genotype file's own aging signal is a weak prior: longevity GWAS are dominated by APOE (Deelen 2019); the parental-lifespan PGS separates extreme deciles by roughly five years of mean lifespan — a population-decile contrast, not an individual prediction (Timmers 2019); genome-wide-significant SNP instruments for epigenetic age acceleration explain 0.47%–4.41% of the respective clock's variance (4 SNPs for GrimAge; Morales Berstein 2022 over the Gibson 2019 / McCartney 2021 GWAS). That is an instrument-strength figure, not a polygenic-score ceiling — a genome-wide PGS would explain more, and its ceiling is not established here — but the ordering still cautions: GrimAge, the strongest mortality predictor among the clocks, is the least genetically instrumentable. The heritability ceiling of longevity is itself contested across a 5x range — below 10% once assortative mating is modeled (Ruby 2018), up to ~50% for intrinsic lifespan once extrinsic mortality is corrected (Shenhar 2026, itself already challenged in preprint: bioRxiv 2026.04.02.716222) — and the distinction that survives every branch of that dispute is that heritability is not predictability from a common-SNP array: even at h2~50%, a consumer file's realized predictive power is bounded by common-variant tagging. So the genotype yields a legitimate low-resolution prior, never a measurement (gen-7). (2) Discovery stays out of scope, on the cited studies' own designs: the longevity/lifespan/healthspan GWAS above ran at n≈300k–1M (Timmers 2019, Zenin 2019); an app-scale paired cohort does not play that game. The product's own pricing agrees (AXES-PLAN §4 on main) — internal context, not external evidence, and marked as such. (3) The valuable cross is established science, not speculation: educational mobility predicts DunedinPACE pace-of-aging and mortality (analysis n=3,101 with methylation data, from a three-generation n=14,106 mobility database), holding under within-family sibling fixed effects and across four alternative clocks (Graf 2024); conscientiousness tracks slower second/third-generation clock aging across cohorts totalling N>6,000 (Stephan 2025); psychosocioeconomic stress and status associate with GrimAge/DunedinPACE acceleration (PMID 38824837). What the perfect axiom therefore contributes to aging research: the deepest behavioral phenotype battery crossed with imported aging measurements (gen-8) and genotype priors (gen-7), generating behavior-aging correlates worth handing to real research — literature-grounded hypothesis work over consented aggregates, never medical advice (charter §9). Edge change this run: the dependency on gen-5 (LLM sequence models) was dropped on ladder grounds — a cited node depending on a conjecture is evidence flowing uphill; the ambition's real dependencies are the boundary (gen-7) and the import door (gen-8).

nodes.claim: LLM-shaped sequence models are the annotation engine of the perfect genetic analysis layer, not its individual-prediction engine: they supply variant-effect, rare-variant and fine-mapping priors that feed an additive polygenic layer, which remains the auditable predictor.
nodes.detail: Fissioned 2026-08-29 per central's 2026-08-28 question (go-7's per-claim-status argument): the empirical no-replicated-win finding now lives at gen-12 and the additivity bound at gen-13; this node keeps the architecture claim the two license. The division of labor: the models' documented strengths are variant-effect and pathogenicity prediction, regulatory annotation and molecular phenotypes (Nucleotide Transformer; Evo, and Evo 2 at 40B parameters claiming zero-shot variant-impact and genome-scale generation, still no individual-level trait claim; Borzoi; AlphaGenome matching or exceeding external models in 25 of 26 VARIANT-EFFECT evaluations — snippet-grade, all molecular, none individual-level trait prediction), and an independent benchmark finds DNA foundation models competitive on pathogenic-variant identification but weaker than specialized models on expression and causal-QTL tasks (Feng 2025). Where they feed the additive layer, measured gains follow while the predictor stays Bayesian-linear: functional annotations improve additive PGS (+14% within-ancestry, up to +34% cross-ancestry — SBayesRC, Zheng 2024); functionally-informed fine-mapping localizes causal variants better (PolyFun, Weissbrod 2020) and sequence-model priors add further (+9.45% additional fine-mapped variants at PIP>0.8 — Borzoi-informed Sniff, 2025 preprint); protein language models raise rare-variant association-DISCOVERY yield (AlphaMissense, Cheng 2023; ESM-class burden scoring, Cell Genomics 2025) — discovery power, explicitly not individual predictive accuracy. One stratified-LDSC caveat rides with the enthusiasm: deep-learning variant-effect annotations add relatively modest information conditional on conservation, coding and regulatory annotations (Dey 2020, measured for DeepSEA/Basenji-class models; the phrasing via the review arXiv 2411.11158) — the annotation engine improves the layer, it does not replace its statistics. This division of labor strengthens gen-2: an additive score over published weight sets is exactly what a device can compute, so keeping prediction on-device costs nothing predictive — the heavy models live on the public annotation side, inside the published weights and priors, never on the per-person path. Conditional written into the claim: if an Epi-PRS-class result is ever independently replicated WITH the gain attributed to the sequence model specifically (gen-12's re-open trigger), this claim widens from 'annotation engine' to 'annotation plus epigenomic-intermediate imputation' — the two-layer architecture, auditable additive predictor with heavy models on the public annotation side, survives either way. nodes.claim: Genetic data is never about one person; the perfect consent model is familial-aware.
nodes.detail: A genome is shared with relatives who never consented. The perfect system therefore publishes only aggregate couplings (never an individual's genetic readout to anyone else), states the kinship fact in consent copy, and treats 'who participates' as itself confidential. This is a design axiom under CHARTER §9, not a limitation to engineer around.

nodes.claim: A SNP genotype file carries a prior on aging, never a measurement of it — the boundary is what the assay reads, not statistics.
nodes.detail: Added by the 2026-08-25 scout; adversarially checked the same run (the check narrowed this node — see below). Every epigenetic clock — Horvath 2013 and Hannum 2013 (first generation, trained on chronological age), PhenoAge 2018 and GrimAge 2019 (second, trained on mortality/morbidity), DunedinPACE 2022 (third, pace of aging) — consumes CpG methylation values from a dedicated methylation array (Illumina 450K/EPIC class). The newest strong aging measures consume plasma proteomics instead: ~200 of ~2,900 Olink proteins predict chronological age at r~0.94 in UK Biobank with external validation (Argentieri 2024), and organ-specific plasma signatures track per-organ aging and disease (Oh 2023). A consumer genotyping array cannot report CpG methylation state: 5mC reads as C to the assay chemistry (amplification erases the mark, but even native DNA reads identically — amplification is sufficient for the loss, not fundamental to it), and the array's probe content interrogates genotype, not methylation. The boundary is probe content and the absent methylation channel, NOT bisulfite chemistry alone: Infinium signal on non-bisulfite-converted DNA still carries some age signal through non-methylation factors ('pseudomethylation', Porter 2025), so the precise claim is that no methylation clock is computable from a 23andMe-class genotype CALL file — the methylation channel is simply absent from it; whether age-correlated signal could be scraped from raw array intensities is a different question about a different input, which consumers do not hold. Imputing methylation from mQTLs does not cross the boundary either: prediction models average a correlation of ~0.20 per CpG (MIMOSA, preprint-grade), and what they recover is by construction the genetic component alone — a polygenic score wearing a clock's costume, discarding exactly the environmental and stochastic signal that makes clocks informative. The adversarial pass hunted for a counterexample (any published method computing a genuine methylation clock from SNP-array genotype data) and found none. So 'what can the genome say about aging' has an architectural answer: the imported genotype supplies a fixed, weak prior (gen-4's figures); the measurement of how a person is actually aging lives in other assays, which the import principle can reach (gen-8) but the genotype file cannot. This sharpens gen-1: 'import, never assay' is not a limitation on the aging ambition, because the thing an assay would add — a clock reading — is itself importable (gen-8).

nodes.claim: The import principle generalizes: the perfect axiom imports any molecular self-measurement the person already holds — consumer methylation files first among them.
nodes.detail: Added by the 2026-08-25 scout; adversarially checked the same run (the check inverted one claim here — see custody paragraph). gen-1's argument was written about genotype files, but its logic — stay on the analysis side, import what consented people already hold — reaches further, and the aging half of the theory needs it to (gen-7: the aging measurement is not in the genotype file). The enabling premise is peer-reviewed fact: consumer-platform methylation cohorts are publication-grade — a TruDiagnostic consumer cohort of n=14,213 serves as a validation cohort in Nature Aging (Chen & Dwaraka 2026, alongside Generation Scotland n=18,672), and the same platform ran a randomized twin diet trial with epigenetic-clock outcomes in BMC Medicine (Dwaraka 2024). The market detail is vendor-grade and labeled so in sources: TruDiagnostic, Elysium Index and myDNAge sell EPIC-class methylation testing to consumers, and TruDiagnostic states customers can download raw data (>850k CpG loci, IDATs on request) — so raw-file import is reported-possible at vendor grade, to be confirmed at vendor-ToS or peer-review grade before gen-2's device-side story is extended to methylation. Given that, actual clock measurements can enter the perfect system by the same door genotypes do; the axiom still never assays. Two consequences. (a) Methylation is a STATE measurement where genotype is a constant, so the perfect import is a longitudinal series of files, not one file — repeat imports are first-class as a property of what the system ACCEPTS from people who already hold such data; per charter §9 this is never a suggestion that anyone test, re-test, or intervene on a schedule — the axiom describes an import door, not a protocol. (b) Custody and consent carry over at FULL strength, not reduced: a methylation array file is also a genotype file at reduced density — genotypes at thousands of SNPs are recoverable from Infinium EPIC data at >98% concordance, enough to identify hundreds of close-relative pairs in a research cohort (MethylGenotyper 2024), and EPIC arrays carry dedicated identity probes — so gen-6's familial-consent logic and gen-2's custody minimization apply to imported methylation files exactly as to genomes.

nodes.claim: Traits the other axioms measure map onto genetic architecture — heritability, polygenicity, effect-size distribution, functional enrichment, correlation structure — not onto gene lists: for psychological and preference traits, 'which genes' has a distribution as its answer.
nodes.detail: Added 2026-08-27, answering the first half of the owner's 2026-08-25 cross-connection question (QUESTIONS.md): how do traits the other axioms measure map onto specific genes? For psychological and preference traits the honest answer is a distribution, not a list. The fourth law of behavior genetics is exactly this claim — a typical behavioral trait is associated with very many variants, each accounting for a very small share of variability (Chabris 2015) — and the omnigenic model gives it a mechanism: interconnected regulatory networks spread heritability across essentially all genes expressed in trait-relevant cells (Boyle 2017; contested in degree but not in polygenicity by Wray 2018; O'Connor 2019 adds the evolutionary why — negative selection purges large effects at critical genes, flattening the effect-size distribution). Twin-scale baseline: across 17,804 traits from fifty years of twin studies, mean reported heritability is ~49% and most traits are consistent with additive-only models (Polderman 2015). The measured shape, per axis-relevant trait: cognitive ability — n=269,867 gives 205 loci, SNP-h2 ~19%, and a polygenic score explaining 4.81% in independent cohorts (Savage 2018); educational attainment — n≈3M gives 3,952 lead SNPs and a PGI predicting 12–16% (Okbay 2022); neuroticism — n=449,484 gives 136 loci (Nagel 2018; the later MVP-led analysis reports 158, Gupta 2024); the other Big Five stood at 2–14 genome-wide-significant loci each as late as 2024 (extraversion 14, agreeableness 3, conscientiousness 2, openness 7 — Gupta 2024) before a 611k–1.14M-sample analysis found 1,257 lead variants with SNP-h2 4.8–9.3%, or 10.5–16.2% corrected for measurement unreliability (ReGPC 2025 — preprint-grade). The saturated contrast case: height, at n=5.4M, needed 12,111 SNPs spread over ~7,209 segments covering ~21% of the genome to capture ~40% of phenotypic variance — and only in European ancestry, 10–20% elsewhere (Yengo 2022). Even the most genetically tractable physical trait saturates to a genome-wide distribution with ancestry-conditional coverage; perfect capability yields a distribution over the genome, never a map of named genes. The gene-list alternative has a documented failure record, not merely an absence of success: 18 historical depression candidate genes performed no better than non-candidate genes across large samples (Border 2019); 1 of 32 replication tests across 12 IQ candidate genes reached even nominal significance (Chabris 2012); and FOXP2's human-specific selection story dissolved as a sample-composition artifact (Atkinson 2018) — while the KE-family FOXP2 mutation stands, which is the right lesson: monogenic DISORDERS of behavior exist; monogenic variation in normal-range traits is what does not. The one honest counterexample class is the pleiotropic hub: CADM2 associates with ~50 behavioral traits from risk-taking to diet (UK Biobank phenome-wide scan, PMID 35867259; Arends 2021) — nameable and mechanistically interpretable, but a hub of a behavioral cluster is a feature OF the architecture (a high-centrality node in the coupling structure), not a gene for a trait. What the perfect cross-connection therefore delivers per trait: an architecture vector — SNP-heritability, polygenicity and effect-size-distribution parameters, functional and cell-type enrichment (stratified LD-score partitioning, Finucane 2015; e.g. intelligence signal concentrating in striatal medium spiny and hippocampal pyramidal neurons, Savage 2018; neuroticism in dopaminergic and serotonergic lineages, Nagel 2018), and the trait's position in genetic-correlation structure (gen-11) — plus the short exception list where a named gene genuinely carries the signal (gen-10). Cell-type and tissue enrichment is itself cross-axis content: it maps question- and test-measured traits onto the body axiom's organs and cell populations without any individual-level data changing hands. Provenance: publisher pages egress-blocked this run; sources record-verified via independent index records; figures snippet-grade unless stated. RE-WARRANTED 2026-09-03 (SCHEMA's go-12 rule; flagged by the review lane's Connected finding and by the health instrument): cen-1 changed on 2026-08-28 from one shared latent space into two linked geometries — a between-person geometry every axiom measures into, plus within-person state geometries with their own loadings, published as aggregate sufficient statistics. This edge survives, and sharpens: a genotype is a per-person constant, so architecture enters the between-person geometry only. A within-person state geometry carries no genotype loading, and an apparent within-person genetic effect is a between-layer quantity moderating trajectory shape (gen-18) — a structural asymmetry against the body axiom, whose bands vary at both levels (bod-2, bod-5).

nodes.claim: Named genes carry cross-axis signal only where a trait is the direct output of a single protein — a percept, a pigment, a secretion; downstream of a mild hedonic percept the signal collapses toward preference and behavior, while aversive toxic percepts carry it through.
nodes.detail: Added 2026-08-27, the second half of the owner's cross-connection answer: where 'specific genes' IS the literal truth. The boundary was sharpened twice by the adversarial pass. It is not 'sensory traits' as a class, and not 'percepts' either (the first draft said percepts, and its own case list violated that — earwax, eye color and hair color are not percepts): it is single-protein DIRECT-OUTPUT phenotypes — traits that are the immediate output of one receptor, enzyme, transporter or regulatory element, whether that output is a percept, a pigment or a secretion. The clean cases: OR5A1 rs6591536 explains >96% of β-ionone odor-sensitivity variation — functionally Mendelian — and flips the odor's reported quality from floral to pungent (Jaeger 2013); ABCC11 rs17822931 determines earwax type outright (Yoshiura 2006); a three-SNP OCA2 intron-1 haplotype explains ~74% of blue/non-blue eye-color variation (Duffy 2007), and the single SNP rs12913832 in HERC2 predicts eye color at ordinal R2 ≈ 0.68, with CC genotypes at ~1% probability of brown eyes (Sturm 2008) — European-cohort quantities, since eye-color variance is itself near-absent in most non-European populations; TAS2R38 PAV/AVI haplotypes explain ~75–80% (source-dependent) of PTC/PROP bitterness perception (Kim 2003); ALDH2 rs671 dominates alcohol flush in East Asian cohorts (association P values down to <1e-4740 reported across GWAS — Science Advances 2023; flushing SNP-h2 ~13% roughly halving to ~6% conditioned on the lead variants — Cho 2023), with rs671 essentially absent outside East Asia; LCT/MCM6 rs4988235 is near-deterministic for adult lactase persistence in Europeans (though NOT for how much dairy anyone consumes — no variance figure for intake is citable); and OR7D4 haplotypes alter androstenone odor perception and valence (Keller 2007 — no numeric variance share citable). The whole exception list is ancestry-conditional in both allele frequency and trait variance — the point gen-9 makes structurally applies here case by case. Downstream of the percept, the fate of the signal splits, and the split is itself lawful. For MILD, HEDONIC percepts the signal collapses on the way to preference and behavior: TAS2R38 genotype→percept is near-Mendelian, but a 72-study systematic review finds bitter-taster status minimally associated with actual food preference and intake — pooled associations small and non-significant across food groups, one modest exception (carbohydrate intake, dz=−0.14; Nutrition Research 2025, PROSPERO CRD42024587607); cilantro soap-taste, the popular 'gene for' story, is really a weak-effect locus — rs72921001 at OR 0.81 per allele with common-SNP h2 ≈0.087, OR6A2 a plausible receptor candidate, never demonstrated causal (Eriksson 2012); MC1R, the textbook red-hair gene, explains only ~73% of red-hair SNP-heritability and most two-variant carriers are not redheads (Morgan 2018); chronotype is decisively polygenic — 351 loci at n=697,828, SNP-h2 ~13.7%, with the top vs bottom 5% of morningness alleles differing by ~25 minutes of accelerometer-measured sleep timing (Jones 2019); habitual coffee intake is polygenic with two interpretable pharmacogenes (CYP1A2, AHR) riding on top (Cornelis 2015), its genetic correlations cohort-dependent (cited at gen-11). But for AVERSIVE, TOXIC percepts the signal carries through to behavior: ALDH2 rs671 is described in the literature as the major genetic determinant of alcohol CONSUMPTION in East Asians — the acetaldehyde flush is punishing enough that the percept-level effect survives into the behavioral phenotype (a similar pattern is reported for CYP2A6 and smoking quantity — noted, not source-verified this run). The adversarial pass supplied this split after catching the first draft asserting collapse and citing ALDH2-on-consumption in the same paragraph; the repaired boundary is predictive rather than descriptive: expect gene-level signal in a behavior only when the intervening percept is aversive enough to dominate hedonic and social modulation. The consequence for the cross-connection: of everything the question, test, body and interest axioms measure, there is a small, enumerable set of items where a genotype genuinely predicts the individual answer — items that ask about the direct output itself (does cilantro taste soapy; how bitter is this; do you flush when drinking; can you smell asparagus metabolites in urine) — and a large remainder where the genome contributes architecture and priors only (gen-9). The perfect axiom knows which side of the boundary each of its crosses sits on and prices the cross accordingly: direct-output items are the highest-value per-genotype pairing anchors the phenotype battery can hold, everything else is population-level architecture. This sharpens que-1 from the genetic side — a bank that wants genetic tractability includes direct-output items on the shared spine (REQUESTS row this run). nodes.claim: A population-level gene–trait coupling is a composite; the perfect cross-connection publishes every coupling with its decomposition — direct effect, genetic nurture, mating structure — because the split is real, measurable, and trait-specific.
nodes.detail: Added 2026-08-27, the third piece of the cross-connection answer: what a gene–trait coupling honestly IS once measured. Four measured facts force the decomposition. (1) For attainment-type traits, a large share of the population-level signal is not a direct genetic effect on the person: the polygenic score built from parents' NON-transmitted alleles carries ~30% of the transmitted score's association with educational attainment (genetic nurture — Kong 2018, 29.9% snippet-grade); within-sibship estimates shrink for EA, cognitive ability and others, with EA SNP-h2 falling 0.13→0.04 within siblings, a 76% attenuation (Howe 2022: 178,086 siblings, 25 phenotypes — snippet-grade figures); EA4's direct effects are roughly half the population PGI association (Okbay 2022); and occupational-status prediction drops 54–57% within families, decomposed as 22–27% indirect parental effects plus 21–27% assortative mating (Akimova 2024). (2) The split is trait-specific, not a law — and for personality it is genuinely unsettled, which the node records rather than resolves: the largest within-family personality analysis (611k–1.14M population, 51k within-family) reports no identifiable within-family reduction in Big Five prediction and minimal confounding from stratification, dynastic effects or assortative mating (ReGPC 2025 — preprint-grade), while a smaller peer-reviewed twin analysis found within-family neuroticism PGS prediction reduced by 80.4% relative to between-family in up to 2,366 DZ pairs (Selzam 2019 — peer-reviewed but with wide uncertainty at that n, and the gap largely closed after adjusting for socioeconomic status). The honest current reading: attainment traits are demonstrably the heavily-confounded class across multiple designs; for personality the biggest data says clean and a smaller peer-reviewed result says otherwise — the perfect system carries the tension as data. Either way, a system that showed one shrinkage number for 'genetics' would be wrong in several directions at once. (3) The genome's connective tissue across traits — genetic-correlation structure (the atlas method, Bulik-Sullivan 2015: 276 correlations among 24 traits from summary statistics alone; joint factor models over that structure, Grotzinger 2019; risk tolerance sharing lead loci with drinking, smoking, speeding and sexual-behavior phenotypes at 46 of 99 loci, Karlsson Linnér 2019; occupational status at rg 0.96–0.97 with educational attainment, Akimova 2024) — is genuinely cross-axis content: it couples traits measured by different instruments at the latent genetic level, computable from published summary statistics without any individual-level data changing hands. But it is partly mating-market artifact: cross-mate phenotypic correlations predict genetic-correlation estimates at R2=74%, and some reported psychiatric rg values are congruent with cross-trait assortative mating alone (Border 2022, Science); the EA–BMI genetic correlation attenuates toward zero within siblings (Howe 2022); and assortative mating biases marker-based heritability estimates themselves (Border 2022, Nature Communications). (4) The coupling also depends on the measurement: the same self-reported coffee-intake phenotype produced genetic correlations with cognition and psychiatric traits that flipped sign or vanished between 23andMe and UK Biobank (2024 GWAS comparison) — ascertainment and item wording change the genetic answer, which binds this axiom's couplings to the questions axiom's measurement discipline and is a direct, citable warning for any self-report-derived phenotype. Consequence: in the perfect system a cross-axis genetic coupling is never published as a bare correlation. It is a decomposed quantity — direct, genetic-nurture and mating-structure components, with a within-family evidence grade and cohort/measurement provenance attached — because whether a coupling is biology or social structure is itself first-class data, and the difference is measurable. This is the honesty constraint on cen-1's shared latent space: genetic coordinates carry decomposition labels or they mislead every axiom they touch. RE-WARRANTED 2026-09-03 (SCHEMA's go-12 rule; flagged by the review lane's Connected finding and by the health instrument): cen-1 changed on 2026-08-28 from one shared latent space into two linked geometries — a between-person geometry every axiom measures into, plus within-person state geometries with their own loadings, published as aggregate sufficient statistics. This edge survives, with a sharper target: publication settled at model level means a coupling's sufficient statistics are INCOMPLETE without this decomposition and its within-family grade, since a consumer cannot recover the split afterwards from a bare correlation and an n. The split is a between-family object and makes no within-person claim. gen-20 extends the same requirement to heritability quantities.

nodes.claim: As of August 2026 no independently replicated demonstration exists of a genomic sequence model beating a tuned polygenic score at individual-level complex-trait prediction: the leading published claim, Epi-PRS, shows near-zero independent uptake and its own simulation ablation keeps the margin with the epigenetic channel zeroed — no real-data ablation isolates the sequence model — and the other published claim, HFS, is likewise unreplicated.
nodes.detail: Fissioned from gen-5 2026-08-29 (central's 2026-08-28 question, go-7's argument) and simultaneously RESOLVED as the named Epi-PRS scout task, via a dedicated scout pass (26 searches, 2026-08-29; publisher domains egress-blocked, so figures are snippet-grade unless marked record-grade — GitHub was directly reachable). (1) The negative finding, restated with fourteen more months of evidence than the original: searched under five framings Aug 2026 plus a fresh Sept 2025–Aug 2026 sweep — no independent replication, no critique or matters-arising, and no benchmark inclusion of Epi-PRS was found anywhere. The absence is now corroborated structurally: three substantial 2026 PGS benchmarks that would have included a working sequence-model method all omit it — a 46-tool harmonized benchmark (Muneeb & Ascher 2026, no sequence-model or deep-learning method included, top performer LDpred2-Lassosum2), PGS-hub (Nature Communications 2026, 13 methods × 36 traits, LDpred2 best single-ancestry), and the 80-phenotype openSNP workflow benchmark (no clear deep-learning winner; 41.2% of comparisons practical ties — snippet-grade) — each crowning a tuned linear method. Independent uptake of Epi-PRS is measurable and near zero (record-grade, from the repository itself): github.com/SUwonglab/Epi-PRS has 1 star, 0 forks, and exactly two outside issues, both from one person and both filed before the PNAS publication date. (2) The attribution, resolved as far as snippets allow: Epi-PRS uses Enformer as its sequence model (record-grade, repo README). The paper reports λ=(auROC−0.5)/0.5 — breast cancer λ 0.3994 vs four genome-wide baselines (LDpred2, PRS-CS, Genotype-GBRT, Genotype-PCA-GBRT) at 0.093–0.2798; T2D λ 0.515 vs 0.077–0.3236 (snippet-grade, medRxiv v1). Back-converted (derived arithmetic, not quoted): auROC 0.6997 vs best-baseline 0.6399 and 0.7575 vs 0.6618 — the '~11–12%' previously recorded is the mean RELATIVE auROC gain (+9.3%, +14.5%). The decisive item is the authors' OWN simulation ablation, stated with both of its halves: with the designed epigenetic effect set to 0%, Epi-PRS, Genotype-GBRT and Genotype-PCA-GBRT achieve similar auROCs and all still beat LDpred2/PRS-CS; and as the designed epigenetic proportion rises, Epi-PRS improves where the other methods do not (both verbatim-verified from the record) — so the sequence model HAS a separable contribution, but only where an epigenetic effect was designed into the simulation, and no real-data ablation isolating it surfaced; the real-data margin therefore has nonlinearity-plus-rare-variants as its undischarged alternative explanation. Design note, this lane's own analytic observation and NOT a published critique: Epi-PRS restricted to 5 significance-selected LD blocks (record-grade — the repository file breast/significant_snp_5e-17.bed lists exactly five blocks, threshold in the filename; per-block breast-cancer auROC 0.5379–0.5917, snippet-grade) against genome-wide baselines — where a selection/leakage critique would land, unresolved from snippets. (3) The adjacent candidates dissolve on classification: arXiv 2509.20702 (Niu et al., v2 2026-03-30, unpublished) embeds FAVOR/ClinVar/GWAS-Catalog annotation TEXT with general-purpose text-LLM embedders to enhance a standard PRS — annotation-assisted PGS, not a sequence model; GENPHIRE (Emory, medRxiv Dec 2025, unpublished) embeds sentences built from risk-allele counts PLUS basic clinical information — downstream of a PRS, clinical covariates in the input, LDpred2 absent from its baselines; PRSformer (bioRxiv Oct 2025, unpublished — flagged by this run's adversarial pass as the strongest in-window nonlinear-beats-linear claim) reports a neighborhood-attention transformer over individual-level GENOTYPES on a private N≈5M cohort outperforming tuned linear and LDpred2 baselines — genotypes, not DNA sequence, so not a genomic sequence model, and an unreplicated preprint on a non-public cohort; it belongs to gen-13's crack, not to this claim. The second published sequence-model claim is Haplotype Function Score (Sei applied per haplotype, eLife 2024, peer-reviewed: +16.1–39.8% cross-ancestry polygenic gains over LDAK across four ancestry test sets) — no independent replication found for it either, which is why the headline negative stands with HFS named rather than by pretending Epi-PRS is alone. (4) Individual-level failure remains directly measured where tested: sequence-to-function models poorly explain inter-individual expression (Sasse 2023 — of 184 genes with known causal variants, Enformer anti-correlated for roughly 43%, snippet-grade; Huang 2023, independent cohort, same conclusion — and Enformer is exactly Epi-PRS's front-end, a standing unanswered objection); the 2025–2026 generation improved, not solved, this (AlphaGenome direction-of-effect OR ~3.0, preprint; chromatin accessibility near its heritability ceiling, expression far below, modality-gap preprint; Dubey & Shen 2026 review concurs). Re-open trigger, inherited from the old gen-5 text: an independent replication that attributes the gain to the sequence model specifically moves this node and widens gen-5's claim. nodes.claim: Common-variant genetic variance for complex traits is predominantly additive, which bounds — without zeroing — the headroom any nonlinear predictor has over a tuned linear polygenic score.
nodes.detail: Fissioned from gen-5 2026-08-29 (central's 2026-08-28 question); two in-window sources added by the same scout pass. The bound, from theory: high additive share is expected under U-shaped allele-frequency distributions regardless of gene-level dominance or epistasis (Hill, Goddard & Visscher 2008). From biobank measurement: across 70 traits in 254,679 unrelated individuals, average variance shares are additive 0.208 of phenotypic, dominance 0.001, epistatic 0.055 (snippet-grade triple; the authors conclude epistasis has a limited role — Hivert 2021). From direct predictive tests, three of them: deep nets did not beat linear models on ~100,000 UK Biobank individuals (Bellot 2018); neural networks fit to simulations plus 28 real UK Biobank traits detect limited nonlinearity and are outperformed by linear regression for both genetic-only and genetic-plus-environment inputs, with apparent nonlinearity attributed to joint tagging under LD (Kelemen 2025 — NEW this run, the most direct published challenge to the nonlinearity premise); and a 2025 benchmark of additive vs dominance-adjusted PGS vs GBDT vs neural nets over simulations plus 10 UK Biobank traits finds the additive PGS robust across most scenarios, degrading only under low polygenicity plus high SNP-heritability plus substantial dominance, and notes dominance contributes ~0.83% of additive heritability on average across >1,000 UK Biobank phenotypes (Bell, Wightman, de Leeuw & Posthuma — preprint, snippet-grade — NEW this run). Plus one CONTRARY result, counted as such rather than absorbed (this run's adversarial pass corrected the first draft, which had folded it into the supporting count): Elgart 2022 reports large RELATIVE gains for nonlinear models with the PRS retained as a feature (up to +100% percentage-variance-explained on some traits, snippet-grade); the absolute bases remain unverified by this lane, and the result is diverse-population-focused — it sits in the crack, not against the bound's existence. The 80-phenotype openSNP benchmark agrees at stress-test grade (PGS workflows win a majority, 41.2% practical ties — snippet-grade; it also reports PRS-tool failure modes, PRSice instability and lassosum collapse on 13 phenotypes, so no clean sweep). The consequence: whatever nonlinearity exists at gene level, the population-level variance a predictor can exploit is predominantly additive, so a linear score captures most of the common-variant ceiling by construction — not a capability gap that closes with model scale. The bound is not a zero: the epistatic share is minor, not absent, and the Epi-PRS/GBRT class of results (gen-12), Elgart 2022's relative gains, and PRSformer — the strongest in-window nonlinear claim, a genotype transformer on a private N≈5M cohort reporting wins over tuned linear and LDpred2 baselines, unpublished and unreplicated (source at gen-12) — all sit exactly in that non-zeroed crack: nonlinear methods CAN beat linear baselines in specific designs, and at N≈5M the data-volume crossover pat-6 theorizes may be coming into range; what has not happened is the replicated sequence-model win (gen-12), and the nonlinear wins that do exist are unreplicated, relative-scale, or on non-public data. nodes.claim: The axiom's contribution to genetic engineering is quantitative, not conceptual: editing and embryo-selection analyses already know their outputs scale with direct-effect fidelity but consume within-family decomposition magnitudes measured on thin data for few traits — the perfect axiom supplies those magnitudes at scale across its battery, plus first gene–trait maps for domains nobody has phenotyped; the constraints engineering otherwise waits on (causal-gene assignment, per-mutation agents, delivery, law) it cannot move, and recording that bound is part of the claim.
nodes.detail: Added 2026-09-01, first half of the owner's 2026-08-27 widening (genetic engineering; §9 bounds how — knowledge-layer contributions over consented aggregates handed to governed research, never procedures). Compressed 2026-09-03 alongside its new falsifier, so the addition does not raise the lane's detail maximum; no source, figure or killed framing was dropped. Two naive forms died before landing and the node records them as what it does NOT say. NOT 'editing has outrun target knowledge': the field locates its clinical bottleneck in per-mutation therapeutic agents, delivery and regulation, not target scarcity (Flugel 2025 — snippet-grade on the scout pass, unreachable on the adversarial pass, held as attributed paraphrase; Chen & Liu 2023, whose 'virtually any substitution, small insertion and small deletion' capability sentence is about PRIME editors specifically), and the capability side is real but in-principle (prime editing could address about 89% of the 75,122 pathogenic variants then in ClinVar — an edit-type arithmetic over ClinVar, not a demonstrated correction rate; Anzalone 2019, snippet-grade). NOT 'the resource refines drug-target success': the measured driver is causal-GENE confidence — genetically supported mechanisms succeed at 2.6x, the effect improving with confidence in the causal gene and largely unaffected by genetic effect size, minor allele frequency or year of discovery (Minikel 2024, abstract-verbatim); the >2-fold concentrates where causal genes are clear and the estimate is sensitive to a tunable trait–indication similarity cutoff (King 2019), over a line originating at 2.0% preclinical → 8.2% approved with 'could double' stated there as projection (Nelson 2015). A behavioral battery over consumer arrays supplies none of that axis. The line is observational with self-acknowledged selection confounds (Paterson 2026, preprint: OR 3.25 [2.79–3.79] pair-level attenuating to 2.79 target-level). 63% (271/428) of 2013–2022 FDA approvals already carried genetic support (Minikel & Nelson 2023, snippet-grade) — a base rate licensing no scarcity inference in either direction; the first draft's 'target knowledge is not scarce' was killed pre-land as a non sequitur that also inverts the authors' own 'far from reaching peak genetic insights'. And variant-to-gene tooling shows a null over a trivial heuristic: locus-to-gene OR 3.14 vs nearest-gene OR 3.08, eQTL colocalization not significantly predictive (2025 benchmark, preprint, snippet-grade) — a null difference, not a failure. For the heritable branch the binding constraint is law and safety: of 106 countries surveyed, 96 had relevant policy documents and 75 of those 96 prohibit heritable human genome editing, 70 outright and 5 with possible exceptions (Baylis 2020, snippet-grade); the same-day reply to the flagship feasibility analysis calls embryo editing unsafe and unproven (Carmi, Greely & Mitchell 2025); and the live landscape is contested in both directions — a multi-stakeholder call for a 10-year moratorium (2025-03-26) against the first venture-funded heritable-editing startups (Preventive Medicine PBC, incorporated May 2025; Manhattan Genomics, reported to have ceased work by end-2025), news-grade items with primary sources still an open scout task. The prohibition is reported as a fact about the world, never a constraint to engineer around. WHAT SURVIVES is quantitative, and the framing is itself the adversarial pass's correction — the first draft claimed the decomposition INSIGHT as the missing input, which the flagship analyses already state. Visscher 2025 (simulations where editing up to 10 common variants cuts lifetime type-2-diabetes prevalence from 10% to 0.2%, snippet-grade via the Nature Genetics research highlight) names winner's curse, population stratification and indirect effects, lists feasibility, safety, variant causality, pleiotropy and epistasis among its simplifying assumptions, and drew an author correction for omitted prior simulations; Turley 2021 runs its embryo-selection simulations on WITHIN-family predictive power precisely because between-family signal is partly gene–environment correlation, which is where its small absolute gains come from (about 2.5 cm expected height, −1.8% absolute risk of idiopathic short stature, best of 10 embryos; the paper urges absolute-not-relative framing); Lencz 2021 measures strategy dependence (relative risk reduction often <10% under high-risk exclusion vs about 50% selecting the lowest-PRS of five viable embryos for schizophrenia). What those analyses consume and cannot get is decomposition MAGNITUDES at breadth: within-family shrinkage and nurture/mating shares are measured for a handful of traits on thin designs (Howe 2022's 178k siblings across 25 phenotypes, Selzam 2019's 2,366 DZ pairs, Akimova 2024 — all at gen-11), and for most of what the other axioms measure no within-family estimate exists at all. The lane's own inference, marked as such: the perfect axiom's engineering contribution is (i) gen-11's decomposed couplings AT SCALE — per-trait direct/nurture/mating magnitudes with within-family evidence grades across the whole battery, the numerical input any honest editing or selection simulation must be parameterized by (REQUESTS row 2026-09-01: consented within-family pairing) — and (ii) first gene–trait maps for domains nobody has phenotyped (inventory-grade interests, gen-3; direct-output percept items, gen-10), where the contribution is existence rather than refinement. What it cannot move — causal-gene assignment, per-mutation agents, delivery, law — is recorded as the bound. REFUTATION CONDITION added 2026-09-03 (the review lane's Effective item, which supplied it): this node falls if a published editing or embryo-selection analysis is already parameterized by within-family decomposition magnitudes at battery breadth — the supply it claims being in hand rather than scarce. Narrowing rather than fatal: a within-family consortium releasing direct-effect estimates across a broad phenotype panel moves the contribution from 'supplies' to 'extends'. nodes.claim: The axiom's contribution to the general understanding of genetics runs on four axes orthogonal to sample size — signal specificity, latent structure, within-person time and integration substrate (gen-16 to gen-19) — while raw locus discovery is a contested depth-versus-breadth tradeoff it neither owns nor needs, because the import principle rides other people's n.
nodes.detail: Added 2026-09-01 as the second half of the owner's 2026-08-27 widening, under Houle 2010's premise that phenotyping must scale with genomics or genetics starves. FISSIONED 2026-09-03 on the review lane's Legible item: the four axes carry their own claims, sources and falsifiers at gen-16 to gen-19, and this node keeps the orthogonality claim and the discovery-scale concession. No source was dropped in the split (van Alten 2025 moved to gen-20, ascertainment being one of its three bases). The tradeoff, both directions. Shallow at scale wins locus counts: 23andMe self-reported depression (75,607 cases / 231,747 controls) meta-analyzed with PGC clinical results and replicated in 45,773 further cases yielded 17 SNPs in 15 regions at n=459,481 (Hyde 2016 — a self-report-plus-clinical meta-analysis, not pure self-report), where a 9-cohort clinical mega-analysis of 9,240 cases found none; and a UK Biobank head-to-head found broad self-declared depression its most tractable discovery phenotype (Howard 2018, near-verbatim). Depth has a measured win in the same trait: CONVERGE's 5,303 deeply homogeneous severe recurrent-MDD cases and 5,337 screened controls, under sparse whole-genome sequencing, replicated two loci (near SIRT1, P=2.53e-10; LHPP intron, P=6.45e-12) where >9,000 heterogeneous cases had yielded nothing, strengthening in the melancholic subset. NEW 2026-09-03, bounding depth from the other side: BIONIC 2026 mega-analysed DSM-defined lifetime MDD, uniformly phenotyped in a homogeneous Dutch population, in 64,941 participants (25.7% cases), reporting ONE novel locus (PALMD rs3818852, P=3.26e-8) at rg 0.89 with PGC-MD — uniform depth at 65k does not approach shallow breadth at 459k for locus counts, and the high rg says the two are largely reading one between-person genetic signal. One caveat this node owes gen-20 and states rather than hides: BIONIC's 25.7% case fraction sits far above population prevalence, so its effective n is not comparable to a population sample of the same size — a depth-versus-breadth comparison run on raw n is itself basis-dependent, which is gen-20's rule applied against this node's own headline comparison. Dahl 2023's 'remains contested' is the field's own framing and this node keeps it; the axiom does not own this axis and does not need it (Eriksson 2010's import principle, gen-3). REFUTATION CONDITION (review item 2): falls if the four axes prove to be functions of n after all — if a deep battery's advantage disappears at MATCHED n against a shallow phenotype. Each child names a narrower falsifier. Provenance: publisher hosts egress-blocked; BIONIC's figures snippet-grade, corroborated across two independent searches.

nodes.claim: Measurement depth buys genetic SPECIFICITY, not signal strength: loosely and strictly defined versions of one construct differ more than twofold in SNP heritability and differ in which loci they find, yet stay highly genetically correlated — so depth changes what a genetic result is ABOUT, not how much of it there is.
nodes.detail: Fissioned out of gen-15 2026-09-03 (review lane's Legible item), carrying the specificity axis and the correction the review's Rigorous item demanded. THE FIGURES, restated correctly. Cai 2020 measured a ladder of depression definitions in one cohort: the three minimal-phenotyping definitions run SelfRepDep 10.96% (SE 0.85%), Psypsy 12.57% (SE 1.18%) and GPpsy 14.34% (SE 0.81%), against LifetimeMDD (DSM-based) at 26.21% (SE 2.15%), rising to 31.95% (SE 2.56%) once recurrence is required. gen-15's old sentence gave '~11% vs ~26%' and defended it 'per the published abstract'; that provenance was false, and the review lane was right to name it — the abstract's own headline is 'the genotype-derived heritability of depression defined by minimal phenotyping is 14% (SE = 0.8%), lower than strictly defined MDD at 26% (SE = 2.2%)', while 10.96% is the paper's SelfRepDep figure, one rung of the body-level ladder. This lane's first draft of the fix over-read in the other direction, asserting that the review's 14% was 'GPpsy, not the minimal phenotype'; the adversarial pass killed that. The abstract labels 14% as minimal phenotyping outright. That GPpsy (14.34%, SE 0.81%) is the definition the headline rounds from is an INFERENCE of this lane's from the matching digits, marked as such and not the paper's labelling. The node therefore states the abstract pair AND the ladder, because the ladder is what shows there is no single minimal-phenotyping heritability to quote. That h2 is basis-relative is itself now a claim, at gen-20. The specificity evidence proper, all Cai 2020: the minimal phenotype sits genetically close to strict MDD (rg 0.81, SE 0.03) and closer still to plain neuroticism (rg 0.84, SE 0.05); its GWAS preferentially finds non-specific loci, needing 80.2% of the genome to explain 90% of its genetic correlations with other traits where strict MDD needs 65.8%; and its PGS predicts well, but the predictive power 'can be explained entirely by large sample sizes rather than by specificity for MDD'. COUNTERWEIGHT, stated at full strength: BIONIC 2026's uniformly deep-phenotyped MDD GWAS correlates with PGC-MD at rg 0.89 (SE 0.048 — the correlation snippet-confirmed, the standard error not), and the sharper form the adversarial pass supplied is that its polygenic scores predict BIDIRECTIONALLY between the deep and the shallow cohort while its within-family analyses indicate minimal confounding. Cross-prediction bounds this node harder than rg alone: depth re-weights a largely shared genetic signal, it does not isolate a disjoint one. RECONCILIATION with gen-3, which holds that a single validated item is a genetic-grade phenotype: Niarchou 2022's one item was validated against separate experimental measures. A well-designed single item is a PRECISE measurement of a NARROW construct; a minimal phenotype is a LOOSE measurement of a BROAD one. What costs specificity is measurement looseness, not item count — which is que-1's validity-at-depth discipline reaching the genetic side. REFUTATION CONDITION: falls if the gaps are artifacts of n rather than of definition — if the genome-fraction and rg-with-neuroticism differences close when the strict and minimal phenotypes are compared at matched sample size. nodes.claim: Many items per person admit latent genetic decomposition — the genetics of a factor nobody measured directly — and what a battery contributes is not decomposability, which existing summary statistics already supply, but the CHOICE of measurement model: an item bank designs the latent structure before the GWAS, where subtraction can only ask what an existing pair of GWAS happens to span.
nodes.detail: Fissioned out of gen-15 2026-09-03, carrying the latent-structure axis. The demonstration: GWAS-by-subtraction recovered a noncognitive-skills factor from educational attainment and cognitive performance, yielding 157 loci and accounting for 57% of the genetic variance in educational attainment (Demange 2021; both figures verbatim-confirmed on an earlier run). The honest caveat, which is what makes this a claim about measurement models rather than a claim about batteries: that decomposition ran on two EXISTING summary-statistics GWAS and needed no new item-level data at all. So the battery's contribution is not that latent genetic factors can be recovered — genomic SEM over published summary statistics does that (Grotzinger 2019, at gen-11) — but that the reachable space of factors is bounded by what has already been GWASed. Subtraction asks 'what is in EA that is not in cognitive performance'; it cannot ask a question whose two arms nobody has run. An item bank inverts the order: the latent structure is specified by the measurement model first, and the GWAS is run on the factor scores it defines, which is int-4's rule (structure derived from measured response structure, never authored as a plausible grid) reaching the genetic side. This is also the axis where gen-3's aggregation result bites — item-level interest heritability ~32% rising to ~48% at factor and ~53% at superfactor level (Lykken 1993, at gen-3) is the same phenomenon measured from the twin side: the factor is a better-measured construct than any of its items, so its genetic signal is larger. REFUTATION CONDITION: falls if the space of factors reachable by subtraction and genomic SEM over already-published summary statistics is not meaningfully narrower than the space an item bank could define — concretely, if for some target factor the lane names, a subtraction over existing GWAS pairs recovers it at comparable rg and comparable loci count to a purpose-measured factor score. That is a runnable test on public summary statistics and does not wait on any InSight data.
sources: Demange PA et al. 2021, Nature Genetics 53(1):35–44, 'Investigating the genetic architecture of noncognitive skills using GWAS-by-subtraction', DOI 10.1038/s41588-020-00754-2, PMID 33414549 — 157 loci; noncognitive factor 57% of EA genetic variance; verbatim-confirmed 2026-09-01

nodes.claim: The within-person time axis works by turning a trajectory into new phenotypes: derived trajectory parameters — slope, area, peak, rebound — are the genetic instrument, not the repeated measurements themselves, and they expose age-varying genetic effects that one-shot phenotyping cannot see.
nodes.detail: Fissioned out of gen-15 2026-09-03, carrying the time axis — and sharpened in the fission, because re-verifying the source changed the claim. gen-15 said repeated measurement 'exposes genetic effects one-shot phenotyping cannot see', which is true but names the wrong instrument. What the framework actually does: from 71,336 participants across six cohorts it estimates TWELVE derived phenotypes per person — the slope and the area under the BMI curve within each of four periods (infancy, early childhood, late childhood, adolescence), plus the age and BMI at the adiposity peak and at the adiposity rebound — and runs GWAS on those, identifying 28 genome-wide-significant variants at 13 loci with age-varying effects, one of them (in DAOA) never previously associated with childhood or adult BMI (Burrows 2024). The repeated measurements are the raw material; the phenotypes are the trajectory parameters fitted through them. Two consequences for the axiom. (1) The design requirement on a battery is not 'ask again' but 'ask often enough, and on a schedule dense enough, to RESOLVE the shape' — a construct measured twice yields a slope and nothing else; peaks and rebounds need the sampling to bracket them. (2) This is the one axis where the genetic axiom has no within-person limb of its own: the genotype is a constant, so what varies is the phenotype's trajectory and the genotype indexes its SHAPE (cen-8 reaches the same conclusion from the portfolio side, calling genetic's value pairing-funded with no within-person half). That is exactly why gen-8's longitudinal import series matters — methylation is a state where genotype is a constant, so the imported series is the only route by which a molecular measurement, rather than a molecular constant, enters the within-person geometry cen-1 now separates. REFUTATION CONDITION: falls if age-varying genetic effects prove to be an artifact of the measurement changing meaning across the age range rather than of the genetic effect changing — longitudinal measurement non-invariance, que-4's grading applied to time. The decisive test is establishing longitudinal invariance BEFORE estimating the age-varying effect; the BMI case is comparatively safe from this (a scale reads the same at 4 and 14) and a self-report construct is not, so the refutation bites hardest exactly where this axiom would apply it.

nodes.claim: Many correlated items are an imputation substrate that multiplies effective sample size, and that sets the admission bar for every new item the battery proposes: it must add information beyond what integration over the items already collected recovers.
nodes.detail: Fissioned out of gen-15 2026-09-03, carrying the integration axis. The demonstration: phenotype integration over already-collected UK Biobank items imputed strictly defined MDD at R2 about 40%, roughly doubling effective sample size (67k observed to 166k effective), with roughly ten-fold GWAS loci and two-fold PRS R2, and specificity preserved rather than traded away (Dahl 2023, figures verbatim-confirmed on an earlier run). The result cuts both ways and this node keeps both edges. It proves the many-items substrate is powerful, and a deep answer corpus natively IS that substrate at item grade — every item is both a phenotype and a predictor of every other. And it sets a bar that most proposed new items fail: if integration over what is already asked recovers the target at R2 40%, a new item earns its slot only by adding information that integration cannot reconstruct. The bar is passable exactly where gen-3 and gen-10 point — domains with no existing items to integrate FROM, which is why inventory-grade interests (no GWAS of an administered interest inventory exists) and the direct-output percept items (single-protein anchors nothing else predicts) are the two item classes this theory keeps asking for, and why generic additions to the bank are not genetic-axiom improvements even though gen-3 says the battery is the scarce asset. This is the discipline that keeps gen-3 from licensing indiscriminate growth: the scarce asset is battery COVERAGE of unspanned domains, not battery size. REFUTATION CONDITION: falls if imputation R2 saturates at a small item set — if integrating over a handful of well-chosen items recovers a target phenotype about as well as integrating over hundreds, the substrate argument stops being an argument for breadth and becomes an argument for a short, well-chosen core, which would leave this node's evidence intact and its consequence wrong. Dahl reports the aggregate result; the saturation curve behind it is the quantity that decides this, and the lane has not seen it.
sources: Dahl A et al. 2023, Nature Genetics 55(12):2082–2093, 'Phenotype integration improves power and preserves specificity in biobank-based genetic studies of major depressive disorder', DOI 10.1038/s41588-023-01559-9, PMC10703686 — R2 about 40%; 67k observed to 166k effective n; about ten-fold loci; about two-fold PRS R2; verbatim-confirmed 2026-09-01

nodes.claim: A banded polygenic score states something about a distribution, not about a person, and the two things that break as the person moves away from the discovery cohort break differently: ORDERING degrades gradually and stays informative, while the MAPPING from score to band can be simply wrong — so a band that travels carries its basis, and the basis is not only genetic position but also the reference distribution, the non-genetic context and, for device-side scoring, the array and imputation coverage the score was computed from.
nodes.detail: Added 2026-09-03 as the honesty constraint gen-2's architecture has been missing: gen-2 sends banded quantities across the wire and never said what a band means. The draft this run began from — 'accuracy decays continuously with genetic distance, so a band without its basis is uninterpretable' — did not survive its own scout pass, and the corrections ARE the claim. (1) ORDERING degrades continuously and is well measured: prediction drops off already within European ancestries and falls in proportion to genetic distance (Privé 2022); accuracy tracks a continuous genetic-distance measure at Pearson r = −0.95 across 84 traits, the furthest genetic-distance decile of European-ancestry individuals runs 14% below the closest, and the closest Hispanic/Latino decile performs like the furthest European one (Ding 2023) — the label is not the unit of meaning, the position is. But degraded ordering is a WEAKER measurement, not a meaningless one: a 269-variant multi-ancestry prostate-cancer score validated in 107,247 cases and 127,006 controls stratifies risk in European, African and Hispanic ancestry men alike, attenuated rather than destroyed (Darst 2022 — design and multi-ancestry validation corroborated this run, the per-group odds ratios NOT, so no figure is stated). (2) GENETIC DISTANCE IS NOT THE ONLY BASIS, and privileging it is now contradicted: individual-level accuracy variation is only weakly predicted by genetic distance and explained comparably well by socioeconomic measures; several immunity-related traits drop near zero at INTERMEDIATE distances; and qualitative trends depend on the metric — for type 2 diabetes precision stays roughly constant while recall increases with genetic distance (Wang 2026). A node saying 'accuracy decays' without binding a metric would be refuted by a published counterexample. (3) THE BAND MAPPING fails categorically rather than gradually, and it is already fragile at zero genetic distance: across 13 traits in 291,273 ancestry-matched individuals, only 0.8% (s.d. 1.6%) of top-decile point estimates have 95% credible intervals contained in that decile (Ding 2022). Ancestry does not make the individual band meaningless — it was already weak, and ancestry adds bias on top. Reference implementations have drawn the conclusion: the PGS Catalog calculator emits no percentile without a declared reference panel and a projection into it (Lambert 2024), and calibrated intervals condition on context, where age, sex and income move accuracy by magnitudes comparable to genetic ancestry (Hou 2024). (4) THE LIMB THAT IS THIS SYSTEM'S OWN: device-side scoring of a consumer array makes the PLATFORM part of the basis — a 313-variant breast-cancer score computed across four arrays and low-coverage sequencing shows platform-specific variability that can reclassify individuals around clinically relevant thresholds (Ho 2025) — and no study was found varying array platform and genetic distance TOGETHER, which is exactly the combination gen-1's import principle forces. CONSEQUENCE: a band is publishable only with (a) its discovery cohort, (b) the reference distribution the percentile was taken against and the person's position in it, (c) the non-genetic context the accuracy is conditional on, (d) the array, imputation panel and realized variant coverage. That belongs in the G1 design record if G1 is ever taken; it is a constraint the architecture must satisfy, not a discovery — requiring a calibration basis is close to the field's engineering consensus and the node says so rather than claiming novelty. A failure mode this node does NOT cover: for gen-10's direct-output items ancestry changes INFORMATION CONTENT, not calibration — an rs671 carrier flushes wherever the discovery cohort was, while rs12913832 is near-monomorphic outside Europe and so carries almost no information there while staying perfectly calibrated. Conflating the two would be a category error, and it bounds the percept anchors' use as calibration references. REFUTATION CONDITION: falls if band mapping proves robust to genetic position — if recalibration against a matched reference moves few people across band boundaries in a large diverse cohort — or if the platform limb proves null, i.e. consumer arrays of differing design agree on band assignment within the uncertainty Ding 2022 already establishes for one platform. Provenance: publisher and repository hosts egress-blocked, so every figure is snippet-grade; Ding 2023, Wang 2026 and Ding 2022 were each corroborated by this lane's own independent searches, and figures the scout reported but the lane could not corroborate (Privé's per-group table, the prostate odds ratios, a platform concordance statistic) are omitted rather than restated.

nodes.claim: A heritability figure is a property of an estimator, a phenotype definition and an ascertainment scheme, never of a trait: each of the three moves it by roughly twofold, so the perfect axiom publishes and consumes no bare h2, and a cross-trait or cross-axis heritability comparison means nothing unless all three are held fixed.
nodes.detail: Added 2026-09-03. This is gen-11's discipline applied to the other quantity this axiom traffics in: gen-11 forbids a bare COUPLING, this forbids a bare HERITABILITY, and it is not the softer claim, because three separately measured axes each move h2 materially — by about 1.4x to 8x depending on the axis and the trait — so comparing two published figures can manufacture a large difference out of nothing. The per-axis magnitudes are stated rather than averaged, the adversarial pass having killed a first draft that claimed 'roughly twofold' for all three. (1) DEFINITION. Cai 2020 measured five definitions of one disorder in one cohort and got 10.96% (SE 0.85%) to 26.21% (SE 2.15%), reaching 31.95% (SE 2.56%) once recurrence is required — a 2.4x spread with the genotypes held constant (the ladder is at gen-16). (2) ESTIMATOR MODEL. How a variant's heritability contribution is assumed to depend on its allele frequency, LD and genotype certainty is a modelling CHOICE, and it is disputed: across 19 traits the LDAK model returns common-SNP h2 on average 43% higher than GCTA and 25% higher than GCTA-LDMS — about 1.4x, the smallest of the three axes — while the same model change moves a published functional-enrichment conclusion from DNase I hypersensitivity sites explaining 79% of SNP heritability to 24% (Speed 2017): the choice changes the scientific conclusion, not merely the level. The sharpest instance is one sample: BIONIC 2026 reports 12.0% (SE 1.4%) by LDSC at an assumed 15% lifetime prevalence and 26.6% (SE 1.1%) by LDAK-REML on individual-level genotypes — 2.2x on the same people and the same phenotype, though the contrast is not a clean isolation of the heritability model, since it also changes the estimation substrate (summary statistics versus individual genotypes) and carries an assumed prevalence. And the same paper's ABSTRACT headlines a third figure, 13.4%, so a reader checking the abstract meets a number matching neither: one sample, one phenotype, three published heritabilities. (3) ASCERTAINMENT, the largest axis of the three and the one the first draft left without a magnitude. Correcting UK Biobank for volunteer bias with inverse-probability weights raises SNP effect sizes and heritability across ten phenotypes: breast cancer 2.59% to 5.12% (about 2x) and type 1 diabetes 0.54% to 4.32% (about 8x) — at a real price the node records with it, an average 62% cut in effective sample size (van Alten 2025). Recruitment sits inside the number — not academic here, since an imported-genome population is volunteer-ascertained twice, once into consumer testing and again into consenting to pair. A fourth axis is the lane's own inference, marked as such: twin-design h2 and SNP-based h2 are different ESTIMANDS rather than competing estimates of one, so part of any missing-heritability gap is definitional; the lane asserts the distinction, not a share. CONSEQUENCE: cen-7's declared object needs a further clause wherever the quantity is heritability-like, and a 'trait X is N% heritable' column crossing axes is uninterpretable unless every entry was computed alike — which across the published literature they are not. REFUTATION CONDITION: falls if the estimator dispute resolves, i.e. if a validated consensus heritability model emerges under which LDAK, GCTA and LDSC agree within their standard errors on the same trait; axis (2) would collapse to a historical caveat and the rule would weaken to definition and ascertainment alone. It does not fall on single traits where estimators happen to agree. Provenance: publisher hosts egress-blocked; Speed 2017 and BIONIC snippet-grade, each corroborated across two independent searches this run.
